title: Effect of taurine supplementation on renal histomorphology in healthy adult male rabbits

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Taurine is a sulphur-containing β-amino acid widely recognized for its antioxidant, osmoregulatory, and cytoprotective properties. Although its renoprotective effects have been extensively documented in pathological conditions, limited data are available regarding its structural impact on physiologically intact renal tissue. The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of long-term graded taurine supplementation on renal histomorphology in healthy adult male rabbits. Twenty-four Hyla breed rabbits were randomly assigned to four groups (n=6 per group): control group without taurine supplementation and three taurine-treated groups receiving 321.675 mg (P1), 643.35 mg (P2), and 965.025 mg (P3) of taurine per day for 11 weeks. Taurine was dissolved in drinking water and administered ad libitum. After the experimental period, kidneys were collected, histologically processed, and stained for quantitative morphometric analysis. Assessed parameters included renal corpuscle diameter and area, glomerular diameter, tubular dimensions, nephron frequency, cellular density, and the relative proportions of glomeruli, tubules, and interstitium. No statistically significant differences were observed among the groups in any evaluated parameter. Although a numerical increase in glomerular diameter and renal corpuscle area was noted in the highest-dose group, no evidence of nephron loss, interstitial expansion, or degenerative alterations was detected. These findings indicate that graded taurine supplementation does not induce adverse structural altering in healthy renal tissue, and supports its structural safety under non-pathological conditions.</jats:p>
